description: Smoke coverage for a pinned income instance. Version 3 differs from version 2 in exactly one pointer: the review-required case now also requires /findings/findings/0/subjectKey. Versions 1 and 2 are left in place unchanged so every historical income-smoke report digest stays reproducible. Version 2 deliberately omitted subjectKey because no production run could supply a subjectScope, so a gate asserting it would have failed every correct release; a scope now reaches the analyzer from the registration, so the assertion is meaningful and is restored. A release pinned to this set must therefore run against a registration carrying a subject scope — that is the point of asserting it, since a run without one publishes findings whose subject key is absent and whose waivers can never carry forward. Every package named here is a synthetic fixture; no scenario references a real borrower package, and no expected borrower value appears anywhere in this file. Assertions are JSON pointers into the assertion document described by InstanceAssertionDocument: the stored analysis result with its findings payload inflated under /findings, which is why a finding's own pointer is doubled. A scenario checks that the answer is shaped correctly, cites its evidence, and does not invent what the parse did not contain — never that it contains a particular number, and never a literal digest, which would break on any legitimate change to subject-key composition. Two cases assert an absence, and an absence is only worth asserting when the fixture makes it reachable: fixture-unsupported-only contains nothing an income contract allows, so a release must refuse it before analysis, and fixture-paystub-unreadable is a compatible paystub with every field MISSING, so a release is asked the question and has nothing true to answer with. Note the coupling this set assumes: a release whose parsed-data contract sets missingFields to REJECT refuses the unreadable paystub rather than reporting on it, and would fail the fourth case for that reason. This set is for releases that tolerate missing fields and are expected to say so.
